command: pnpm exec node --env-file=.env node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.integration.config.ts tests/integration/databases-s5.test.ts

scope.controlPlaneDatabase: real PostgreSQL in an independent random s5databases_* schema with the current migrations
scope.http: authenticated Fastify/Nest injection, real transformed DTOs and public responses
scope.admissionAndFences: production ServiceCommands, DatabaseCommands, Storage write ledger, TaskRepository leases and SQL guards
scope.kubernetesAndEngineAuthentication: controlled controller, PVC and database-authentication facts; no live application database engine or Kubernetes call
scope.keyMaterial: independent temporary master key file with mode 0600, removed after the suite; no production key read or modified
scope.cleanup: closed API, dropped only the dedicated test schema, restored process-local environment variables and removed temporary fixture key directory

cases.name: S5 template drafts and generated database identities lists fixed template versions and renders previews without allocating any service, credential, task or volume
S5 template drafts and generated database identities creates exactly one postgresql template draft for concurrent HTTP retries and never returns its generated password
S5 template drafts and generated database identities creates exactly one redis template draft for concurrent HTTP retries and never returns its generated password
S5 template drafts and generated database identities rejects unknown versions, password injection and mixed configuration/template sources without allocating identities
S5 template drafts and generated database identities permits a template draft when storage observations are stale, while its preview clearly marks publication as blocked
S5 database credential and first-data protection rejects a changed exact engine version in the original database snapshot even when its image and major version match
S5 database credential and first-data protection rejects database initialization credentials as generic environment secrets and forbids ordinary credential deletion
S5 database credential and first-data protection persists the original postgresql credential fence before a PVC response or successful initialization and permits equivalent master-key rewrapping
S5 database credential and first-data protection persists the original redis credential fence before a PVC response or successful initialization and permits equivalent master-key rewrapping
S5 database credential and first-data protection keeps database command, image, replica and data-mount changes out of ordinary configuration updates while allowing resource tuning
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention previews and saves same-environment bindings as drafts without deploying, rejecting foreign targets and variable conflicts

S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention pins private Service UID, credential content revision and output mapping in a publication instead of reading the later binding draft
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention blocks provider removal for an unpublished detach until a new consumer publication replaces the original reference
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention serializes provider deletion against binding admission (overlap) so both cannot be accepted
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention serializes provider deletion against binding admission (binding_first) so both cannot be accepted
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention serializes provider deletion against binding admission (deletion_first) so both cannot be accepted

S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention retains the original database, volume, PVC and credential identity after its provider is deleted at the metadata boundary, and forbids reassigning it
S5 database bindings, immutable publications and provider retention keeps a TCP-ready provider unavailable to consumers when authentication or Redis persistence evidence fails

correctionsValidated: Template parameters ignore undefined optional DTO fields, while actual unknown, unsupported and null parameters remain rejected.
Database binding mappings normalize undefined optional DTO fields before preview/save; empty, null, unsupported and unknown actual outputs remain rejected.
Database snapshot identity compares exactVersion in addition to image, major version, template version and original credential reference/content revision.
The parent-owned migration now binds every non-null DatabaseInstance.serviceId to originalServiceJson.id, rejecting reassignment after the original provider has been deleted.

attemptHistory.finding: DTO undefined fields blocked HTTP template/binding commands; exactVersion comparison was missing; two fixture requests needed the documented query/drain preconditions.
After a drained provider Service was deleted, the prior SQL guard allowed a null serviceId to be reassigned to another same-environment database Service.
All cases passed with the latest parent-owned origin guard and strict invalid-input regressions.

limits: Controller health and database authentication/persistence checks use controlled facts and are not live PostgreSQL/Redis or K3s acceptance.
The consumer publication helper advances the real publication pointer using a controlled task outcome; it does not deploy an application Pod.
Provider retention is verified at the SQL metadata boundary after a controlled completed drain, not by deleting a live StatefulSet.
No real backup, restore, network exposure, disk durability, capacity isolation or data recovery is certified here.
Real A/B cluster acceptance and the main database migration are separate work owned by the parent agent.
